capabilities.title: Run offline batch generation with the vLLM LLM class
capabilities.summary: Instantiate LLM once, configure SamplingParams, and batch-generate from many prompts in a single script.

when: Running high-throughput batch generation from an open-weights / Hugging Face LLM in a single script with no server
Generating from many prompts or several independent conversations at once
Producing generations as one step of a larger task (evaluation, labeling, dataset construction)
avoid_when: The model must be called from app code or multiple clients — run a persistent server instead

The task is to fine-tune / compute gradient updates on the weights (including training LoRA adapters) — use a trainer (transformers Trainer, peft, trl), then load the trained model back into vLLM to serve/evaluate it

expected_outcomes: Submitting many prompts in one generate() call is far faster than looping one prompt at a time, thanks to continuous batching

steps: Instantiate the engine once: llm = LLM(model=<hf-repo-id-or-local-path>); reuse it for every batch — re-instantiating reloads weights and re-allocates the KV cache. Add trust_remote_code=True for models with custom modeling code; set max_model_len to cap the KV cache and dtype/quantization as needed.
Build a list of prompt strings, or use llm.chat(messages) for instruction-tuned/chat models so the model's chat template is applied; pass a list of message-lists to batch multiple conversations.
Configure SamplingParams (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, n): temperature=0 gives greedy deterministic decoding; n>1 returns several candidates per prompt.
Call llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params) (pass use_tqdm=False in scripted runs); it returns one RequestOutput per input prompt in input order.
Read each result's generated text at output.outputs[0].text.

validation: generate() returns exactly one RequestOutput per input prompt, in the same order, and output.outputs[0].text is non-empty for each
recovery: OOM at load or during generation -> lower gpu_memory_utilization or set max_model_len to shrink the KV cache; if it still doesn't fit, quantize (see quantize-to-fit-vram)
Model fails to load because it ships custom modeling code -> pass trust_remote_code=True

capabilities.title: Serve a model over an OpenAI-compatible API with vllm serve
capabilities.summary: Launch a persistent vllm server, wait until it is healthy, confirm the model, and smoke-test a chat completion.

when: The model must be called from app code or by multiple clients over a persistent HTTP API
avoid_when: The task is a one-shot batch job in a single script — use offline LLM-class inference instead
The task is to fine-tune the weights — train first, then serve the result

steps: Run vllm serve <model>, setting --max-model-len and --gpu-memory-utilization as needed; optionally --served-model-name <alias> and --host/--port (default 0.0.0.0:8000). The process stays in the foreground until killed.
Wait until the server reports healthy on /health, then confirm the model appears at GET /v1/models — run scripts/wait_for_server.sh.

Send a request to /v1/chat/completions (messages list, reply at choices[0].message.content) or /v1/completions (raw prompt, reply at choices[0].text); the openai Python client works by pointing base_url at http://localhost:8000/v1.
Verify end-to-end with scripts/smoke_completion.py.
MCP fallback: if a serve flag or endpoint you need is not in references/online-serving.md, resolve the libraryId via context7 (libraryName="vllm") and query the docs.

validation: /health reports healthy and GET /v1/models lists the served model id (scripts/wait_for_server.sh passes)
A /v1/chat/completions request returns a non-empty choices[0].message.content (scripts/smoke_completion.py prints a response)
recovery: KV-cache allocation OOMs at startup -> lower --max-model-len and/or --gpu-memory-utilization
Model's tokenizer has no chat template -> pass --chat-template (path or inline Jinja)
Model ships custom modeling code -> add --trust-remote-code

capabilities.title: Probe free VRAM before loading or serving a model
capabilities.summary: Run check_vram.sh to read per-GPU free VRAM from nvidia-smi and decide whether a model fits.

when: Before launching vllm serve or instantiating LLM, to catch OOM early
Deciding whether a model fits at full precision — the precondition for quantization or multi-GPU parallelism

steps: Run bash scripts/check_vram.sh to probe nvidia-smi for free VRAM per GPU; it warns when free VRAM falls below a threshold.
Compare reported free VRAM against the model's full-precision footprint to decide: load at full precision, quantize to fit, or shard across GPUs.

recovery: nvidia-smi missing or no GPU visible -> the run has no usable GPU; fix GPU allocation / CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES before loading a model

capabilities.title: Choose a vLLM quantization method by GPU support and goal
capabilities.summary: Map VRAM-bound vs throughput-bound goals and checkpoint availability onto AWQ/GPTQ/FP8/BitsAndBytes/GGUF.

when: Deciding which quantization method to use for a model that does not fit at full precision
Choosing between a pre-quantized checkpoint and on-the-fly quantization
avoid_when: The model fits in available VRAM at full precision — quantization adds dequantization overhead and can cost quality for no benefit

steps: Weight-only 4-bit (AWQ, GPTQ, W4A16) shrinks weights ~4x — best when VRAM-bound and you want a larger model on one card.
Weight+activation 8-bit (FP8, INT8 W8A8) keeps more accuracy — best when throughput-bound on a card with FP8 tensor cores (Ada/Hopper, compute capability 8.9+) or INT8 (Ampere+).
BitsAndBytes quantizes in-flight with no pre-quantized checkpoint (set quantization="bitsandbytes" and load_format="bitsandbytes") — fastest path to any 4-bit run, but slower at serve time.
GGUF imports llama.cpp checkpoints (experimental); supply the matching HF tokenizer because GGUF files carry no vLLM-compatible one, and merge sharded GGUF files first.
AWQ is under-optimized vs FP8/INT8 in vLLM — prefer it for VRAM savings, not peak throughput.

For most pre-quantized Hub checkpoints vLLM auto-detects the format, so you need not pass quantization at all; pass it (or --quantization) only to force a specific method/kernel, e.g. awq vs awq_marlin.

capabilities.title: Quantize a model to fit it on a smaller GPU
capabilities.summary: After confirming full precision does not fit, pick a method and load/serve with the quantization flag, tuning memory if it still OOMs.

when: A model does not fit in available VRAM at full precision and must run on the available GPU(s)
avoid_when: Memory is not the constraint — load/serve at full precision; quantization adds dequantization overhead and can cost quality for no benefit
You need peak throughput and have VRAM headroom — full precision or FP8/INT8 outperforms weight-only 4-bit methods

expected_outcomes: Weight-only 4-bit shrinks weights ~4x and FP8 reclaims ~half the weight memory, freeing VRAM to fit the model or enlarge the KV cache

steps: Confirm the precondition: run scripts/check_vram.sh and verify the full-precision weights genuinely don't fit; otherwise load at full precision.
Pick a method by checkpoint availability and goal (see quantization-method-selection): pre-quantized AWQ/GPTQ/FP8/GGUF, or on-the-fly BitsAndBytes when no quantized checkpoint exists.
If no pre-quantized checkpoint exists and you want a durable one, quantize your own with AutoAWQ / GPTQModel / LLM Compressor and point vLLM at the output dir.
Load/serve with --quantization <method> (or quantization= in the LLM constructor), or load a pre-quantized checkpoint that vLLM auto-detects; for BitsAndBytes also set --load-format bitsandbytes.
Optionally enable a quantized KV cache to free more VRAM.
If it still OOMs, lower --gpu-memory-utilization / --max-model-len.

validation: The startup log reports the quantization method/kernel actually selected
The model loads/serves without OOM and check_vram.sh confirms it now fits
recovery: Still OOM after quantizing -> lower --gpu-memory-utilization and --max-model-len, or enable a quantized KV cache
FP8 fails on the GPU -> the card lacks FP8 tensor cores (needs Hopper/Ada, compute capability 8.9+); use AWQ/GPTQ INT4 instead
Throughput too low with AWQ -> AWQ is under-optimized in vLLM; re-quantize to FP8/INT8 if the GPU supports it

capabilities.title: Scale a model across multiple GPUs with tensor/pipeline parallelism
capabilities.summary: When a model is too large for one GPU, shard with tensor parallelism within a node and add pipeline parallelism only across nodes.

when: A model is too large to fit on a single GPU
Reducing memory pressure within a layer to leave more room for the KV cache
avoid_when: The model already fits on one GPU — parallelism adds cross-GPU communication overhead that buys nothing

steps: Confirm the precondition: the model doesn't fit on one GPU (scripts/check_vram.sh); otherwise keep the single-GPU path.
Set --tensor-parallel-size (CLI) or tensor_parallel_size=N (LLM) to the number of GPUs on one node — TP shards parameters within each layer.
Add --pipeline-parallel-size only when spanning multiple nodes; rule of thumb: TP = GPUs per node, PP = number of nodes.
For multi-node, launch a Ray cluster first, then serve across it.
Control which physical devices are used via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; do NOT call torch.accelerator.set_device_index() before vLLM initializes.
Verify all shards loaded and the server reports healthy (scripts/wait_for_server.sh).

validation: All shards load and the server reports healthy on /health with the model listed at GET /v1/models (scripts/wait_for_server.sh passes)
recovery: A shard fails to load or the server hangs -> ensure the visible GPU count matches --tensor-parallel-size and devices are exposed via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
Single-node multi-GPU still OOMs -> the model may need multiple nodes; add pipeline parallelism across a Ray cluster

capabilities.title: Constrain generation to JSON, a choice set, regex, or grammar (guided decoding)
capabilities.summary: Attach a guided-decoding spec to SamplingParams (offline) or the request (online) to force schema-valid output.

when: The task needs machine-parseable output: valid JSON, a fixed choice set, a regex, or a grammar
Doing classification or extraction where the answer must conform to a schema
avoid_when: Free-form natural-language output is acceptable — guided decoding adds constraint overhead for no benefit

steps: Offline: build a GuidedDecodingParams (choice=[...], a JSON schema, a regex, or a grammar) and pass it as SamplingParams(guided_decoding=...).
For a fixed label set use GuidedDecodingParams(choice=[...]); for structured records use a JSON schema.
Online: send the equivalent guided-decoding field on the /v1/chat/completions or /v1/completions request.
Call generate() (or hit the endpoint) and read the constrained text from output.outputs[0].text, then parse the JSON/choice.

validation: The returned text parses as the requested type: valid JSON against the schema, or exactly one of the allowed choices
recovery: Output does not conform -> confirm guided_decoding is actually attached to the SamplingParams/request rather than only described in the prompt
